les: Wol op die skaap, trui in die winkel
kaps_punt: Goedere: Grondstowwe (primêre produkte), Vervaardigde goedere (sekondêre produkte)

items.bewering: 'n Trui hang in 'n winkel, maar die wol het op 'n skaap gegroei.
items.bron: NWGA (Nasionale Wolkwekersvereniging), 'The ABCs of wool processing', nwga.co.za/the-abcs-of-wool-processing/: wool shorn from sheep, then processed and knitted or woven into garments.

items.bewering: Elke jaar skeer 'n boer die wol van die skaap af.
items.bron: NWGA, 'The ABCs of wool processing': traditionally shorn once a year, many producers now on 8- or 6-month intervals; an AWI survey reported 79% of producers shearing every 12 months. The sentence says sheep are shorn every year, not only once a year, so it holds under either schedule.

items.bewering: Die wol lê dan in 'n groot sak en is nog net wol. Niemand het dit al in iets anders verander nie.
items.bron: NWGA, 'The ABCs of wool processing': 'Wool is shorn, classed and baled on the farm and then transported to brokers'; scouring, carding, combing and spinning all happen later, mostly abroad. Classing (sorting) and baling do not change the wool into anything else.

items.bewering: Iets wat so uit die natuur kom, noem ons 'n grondstof.
items.bron: American Heritage via Wordnik, 'raw material': 'an unprocessed natural product used in manufacture'; WordNet: 'material in its unprocessed, natural state'; Dutch 'grondstof' (webwoordenboek.nl): unprocessed material used to make products.

items.bewering: Boere plant en oes party grondstowwe en vissers haal ander uit die see. Myners haal erts uit die grond en werkers kap bome in 'n bos.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Primary sector of the economy': extraction and production of raw materials, 'farming, logging, fishing, forestry and mining'; Wikipedia, 'Economic sector': 'miners, farmers and fishermen'.

items.bewering: Iemand moet die wol eers tot 'n lang draad spin. Daarna word daardie draad ry op ry tot 'n trui gebrei.
items.bron: NWGA, 'The ABCs of wool processing' (spinning draws the sliver into yarn and adds twist, then knitting or weaving); Wikipedia 'Knitting' and NPTEL knitting basics: knitted fabric is built from consecutive horizontal rows (courses) of loops. Note: industrially the wool is first scoured, carded and combed before spinning. The sentence leaves those steps out but does not deny them, and hand spinners do spin unwashed fleece ('spinning in the grease', Spin Off magazine, motherearthnews.com). It is incomplete but not false.

items.bewering: Die trui is nou iets heel anders as die wol waarmee begin is. Ons noem so 'n nuwe ding 'n vervaardigde goed.
items.bron: Britannica, 'manufacturing': any industry that makes products from raw materials by manual labour or machinery; Wikipedia 'Economic sector': secondary sector transforms raw materials into goods, e.g. 'textiles into clothing'.

items.bewering: Vervaardigde goedere word meestal in 'n fabriek of 'n werkswinkel gemaak.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'manufacture': the making of products, especially with machines, in factories; Britannica 'manufacturing' also includes manual labour (handicraft), which a workshop covers. 'meestal' leaves room for home-made goods.

items.bewering: Mense koop en verkoop grondstowwe sowel as vervaardigde goedere. 'n Boer verkoop sy wol en 'n winkel verkoop die trui.
items.bron: NWGA, 'The ABCs of wool processing': raw wool goes to brokers and is 'sold on auction and finally shipped to various countries for processing'; mecardo.com.au, 'South African merino clip': more than 90% of the SA clip is exported raw.

items.bewering: 'n Grondstof word ook 'n primêre produk genoem.
items.bron: Economics Help (economicshelp.org), primary products: goods obtained by cultivating or extracting raw materials with no manufacturing step; Wikipedia, 'Primary sector of the economy': 'Industry of raw materials and unprocessed food'.

items.bewering: Primêr is die eerste stap waar iets uit die natuur gehaal word.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Economic sector' and 'Primary sector of the economy': the primary sector is the retrieval and production of raw materials, which the secondary sector then transforms, so extraction is the first stage of the goods chain. The 'eerste' here is the order of steps in production, not a historical first.

items.bewering: 'n Vervaardigde goed word 'n sekondêre produk genoem.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Secondary sector of the economy': secondary sector = manufacturing that produces finished, usable products; Wikipedia, 'Economic sector'.

items.bewering: Sekondêr is al die maakwerk saam en dit maak nie saak hoeveel keer 'n goed verander nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Economic sector': the secondary sector 'involves the transformation of raw materials or intermediate goods into goods', e.g. steel into cars. Its industry list puts flour, baking, metal refining and steel all in the secondary sector, and there is no further goods sector (the tertiary sector is services). So every processing stage counts as secondary.

items.bewering: Die twee woorde sê niks oor hoe goed of hoe belangrik 'n goed is nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Three-sector model' and 'Economic sector': the sectors are defined by the kind of activity (extraction vs transformation) and the model does not rank them by importance.

items.bewering: Koring word tot meel gemaal en bakkers bak brood daarvan.
items.blok: Nog drie pare om self na te loop
items.bron: Warburtons, 'Wheat to bread' (warburtons.co.uk) and Brennans, 'How bread is made': grain is ground into flour in a mill, then mixed into dough and baked at a bakery.

items.bewering: Ystererts kom uit 'n myn en 'n fabriek maak staal daarvan.
items.blok: Nog drie pare om self na te loop
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Iron ore': 98% of mined iron ore is used to make steel (by way of pig iron); ArcelorMittal SA, 'Iron making' (arcelormittalsa.com): Vanderbijlpark and Newcastle works turn ore from Sishen, Beeshoek and Thabazimbi mines into iron and then steel in one integrated works.

items.bewering: Hout kom van 'n boom en 'n houtwerker maak 'n stoel daarvan.
items.blok: Nog drie pare om self na te loop
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Economic sector': logging/forestry is primary and turning materials into goods is secondary; Wikipedia, 'Secondary sector of the economy' lists handicraft and furniture-type manufacture. A woodworker makes furniture from timber, which is ordinary meaning.

items.bewering: 'n Fabriek maak staal uit ystererts en staal is dus self 'n vervaardigde goed.
items.blok: Van ystererts tot staal tot 'n motor
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Secondary sector of the economy': steel and metal refining appear in the secondary-sector industry list; ArcelorMittal SA, 'Iron making': ore is reduced in blast furnaces and then made into steel at the works.

items.bewering: 'n Fabriek wat motors maak, gebruik daardie staal as materiaal. Die motor is ook 'n vervaardigde goed en albei is sekondêre produkte.
items.blok: Van ystererts tot staal tot 'n motor
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Economic sector': the secondary sector transforms 'raw materials or intermediate goods into goods, as in steel into cars'.

items.bewering: So kan iets wat een fabriek maak die materiaal van 'n ander fabriek wees.
items.blok: Van ystererts tot staal tot 'n motor
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Economic sector': 'intermediate goods' are inputs to further secondary production (steel into cars, textiles into clothing).

items.bewering: grondstof: Iets wat uit die natuur kom en nog nie verander is nie.
items.bron: American Heritage via Wordnik: 'an unprocessed natural product used in manufacture'; WordNet: 'material in its unprocessed, natural state'; German 'Rohstoff': unprocessed material in its natural state. In trade usage the word is sometimes stretched to cover processed inputs, but the lesson consistently avoids calling steel a grondstof and calls it 'materiaal' instead, so the narrow definition is applied consistently.

items.bewering: primêre produk: Nog 'n naam vir 'n grondstof, want dit is die eerste stap.
items.bron: Economics Help, primary products (cultivated or extracted, no manufacturing step); Wikipedia, 'Primary sector of the economy'. 'eerste stap' means the order in the production chain, as in the study text.

items.bewering: vervaardigde goedere: Goedere wat mense maak deur grondstowwe of ander goedere te verander.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Economic sector': 'transformation of raw materials or intermediate goods into goods'; Britannica, 'manufacturing'.

items.bewering: sekondêre produk: Nog 'n naam vir 'n vervaardigde goed, hoeveel keer dit ook al verander is.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Economic sector' and 'Secondary sector of the economy': all transformation of raw or intermediate goods is secondary; flour, bread, steel and cars are all listed there.

items.bewering: ystererts: Klip uit 'n myn waarin daar yster is.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Iron ore': 'rocks and minerals from which metallic iron can be economically extracted', mostly iron oxides (hematite, magnetite). The definition leaves out 'economically' and the fact that the iron is bound in compounds, but every iron ore is a rock containing iron, so the simplification is true. The words 'uit 'n myn' exclude ordinary iron-bearing rocks well enough at this level.

opsomming: All 25 checkable claims are confirmed against sector definitions, the NWGA's wool chain and iron-ore and steel sources; the two 'eerste stap' uses mean production order rather than a historical first, the lesson contains no analogy, and its only simplifications are true ones (spinning before knitting without mentioning washing and carding, and iron ore without 'worth mining').
